Subject: SKU harmonization + fallback policy across AWS / Azure / GCP marketplaces

Team + AWS,

Following up from our GTM sync — attaching the first pass SKU mapping (sku_mapping_v1.xlsx) and a suggested canary-region matrix. Key asks:

- We need to agree on a minimum cross-cloud SKU surface that keeps procurement simple for customers (3 tiers: Starter / Scale / Enterprise) while not duplicating operational SKUs that only make sense on a single cloud.
- Define a fallback policy when a SKU isn't available in a region/cloud (e.g., route to compatible SKU on another cloud, provide billing equivalence, or mark as unavailable).
- Co-sell triggers: which SKUs should auto-qualify for co-sell and what marketplace listing requirements (pricing, SAML, private offers) we must meet per cloud.

Proposal highlights (see attached excel for mapping):
- Harmonize on 3 packaging tiers with aligned feature bullets. Keep price points cloud-native but within a 10% band.
- AWS: support private offers + Bring-Your-Own-License (BYOL) for Dedicated customers; list Starter/Scale in AWS Marketplace as meter-based SKUs for procurement simplicity.
- Azure: emphasize Enterprise SKU with reserved term discounts and marketplace plan linking for Azure EA customers.
- GCP: surface Starter/Scale for self-serve, Enterprise via partner-private-offer.

Requests:
1) Ben — can you validate the cost/throughput implications of bundling token-burst allowances into Starter vs Scale?
2) Karthik — prioritize which regions we should pilot per cloud for a 60-day canary (I suggested us-east-1, eu-west-1, asia-southeast1).
3) Naomi — any co-sell policy gotchas on our side (contracts/legal/visibility) we should surface before listing?

AWS — any marketplace constraints we should be aware of for the proposed fallback policies (private offers cross-region, billing equivalence)?

Thanks,
Sooj

--
Soojinn Lee

Quick read — nice work. A few notes from infra/ops cost perspective:

- Starter should be capped on concurrent tokens and be single-GPU serving to keep unit economics predictable. Scale should include autoscale to multi-GPU and a separate token billing breakpoint. Enterprise is custom pricing.
- Bundling a small prefix cache/blended latency SLA into Starter makes it attractive and avoids early fallback churn. That adds ~6-8% to infra cost; we can offset via a 7% price delta in the excel.
- Fallback policy: if a SKU isn't available in region X, prefer cross-region routing within the same cloud before cross-cloud to preserve identity, latency, and co-sell attribution. Cross-cloud fallback should be a last resort and requires a clear note on billing equivalence in the marketplace listing.

I'll attach a short cost delta sheet tomorrow. Agree on the 3-tier harmonization.

-ben

Thanks — short update from listing ops perspective: 

- Pilot regions recommendation: US-EAST-1 (AWS), EU-WEST-1 (Azure), ASIA-SOUTHEAST1 (GCP). These provide representative procurement patterns and latency profiles.
- Listing constraints: AWS requires distinct ASIN-like plan IDs per pricing model; Azure requires plan linking to offer IDs; GCP supports SKU-level metering but has stricter labels for private offers. I captured specific IDs mapping in the attached sheet.
- Action: I'll create a canonical mapping of plan_id -> redwood_sku for each cloud and add lifecycle tags (canary, GA, deprecated). We should aim to have private-offer templates ready for Enterprise by EOW.

Question for AWS PM: can private offers be scoped to region and still count as co-sell-eligible? If not, we need to change the fallback ordering.

-karthik

Hi Soojin / team,

Thanks for the detailed mapping. A few clarifications from AWS Marketplace: 

- Private Offers: they can be scoped to specific accounts and offer terms, but co-sell eligibility is evaluated at the offer level. If a private offer is region-scoped but references the same offer ID, it can still be co-sell-eligible — you just need the co-sell metadata present on the offer. Work with your Partner Development Manager to ensure the offer metadata is set.
- Cross-region vs cross-cloud fallback: co-sell attribution is best preserved when using same-cloud cross-region fallbacks. Cross-cloud fallbacks will make attribution messy unless you implement an explicit attribution token passed as part of the order flow.
- Billing equivalence: AWS supports price-matching via private offer adjustments, but you must surface that clearly in the offer terms.

Recommend: Pilot as proposed (us-east-1, eu-west-1, asia-southeast1) and keep the fallback order: same-region same-cloud -> cross-region same-cloud -> cross-cloud only if feature parity exists.

Happy to hop on a short call with Partner Dev and Karthik to review offer metadata.

Thanks everyone — quick decision log and action items below (so we have a single source of truth):

Decision summary:
- Adopt 3-tier SKU harmonization (Starter / Scale / Enterprise) with cloud-native price bands (<=10% variance).
- Fallback policy agreed: same-region & same-cloud -> cross-region same-cloud -> cross-cloud (only if parity confirmed). Cross-cloud fallback requires explicit billing equivalence note in listing.
- Pilot regions: us-east-1 (AWS), eu-west-1 (Azure), asia-southeast1 (GCP). 60-day canary.
- Co-sell trigger: Scale + Enterprise SKUs are primary co-sell candidates; Enterprise must have private-offer templates ready before GA.

Action items:
- Ben: finalize cost-delta sheet and confirm infra delta for Starter vs Scale (due 2026-09-10).
- Karthik: build canonical plan_id -> redwood_sku mapping and lifecycle tags, draft private-offer templates for AWS Enterprise (due 2026-09-14).
- Naomi: legal to confirm visibility clauses needed for co-sell contracts and any procurement checklist items for Acme (due 2026-09-11).
- Soojin: schedule Partner Dev sync with AWS to finalize co-sell metadata (meeting invite sent).

AWS / Acme — appreciate the quick clarifications. We will loop you in as plan_ids and offer templates become available.

Sooj
